newsitem.title: CHINA: China yr/yr M2 growth down 8 pct points in April.
newsitem.headline: China yr/yr M2 growth down 8 pct points in April.

text.p: Growth in China's broad M2 money supply was down eight percentage points at the end of April, compared with the end of April 1996, the China Securities on Tuesday quoted the central bank as saying.
Year-on-year M2 growth was 28.5 percent at the end of April last year.
Growth in M1, or currency in circulation plus current business deposits, was up five percentage points at the end of April compared with the year before, China Securities said.
Year-on-year growth in M1 at the end of April 1996 was 13.7 percent.
The main reason for the steady growth in M1 was an increase of more than 7.0 billion yuan in the value of loans made in February and an 16.0 billion yuan increase in March, the newspaper said.
After two interest rate cuts in 1996, enterprises were reluctant to put their funds in fixed deposits, causing a rise in production investment, it said.
Stable general demand was a cause of the continued decline in M2 growth, as growth in the demand for money had been restrained, it said.
